evidence.finding: Lifetime measurements support a donor-to-surface inverse-fourth-power nonradiative transfer model.
The measured distance law changes with gold size and plasmon overlap; 80 nm gold quenches more strongly than 15 nm in this system.
evidence.reason: No verified fitted characteristic distances for these donor/acceptor systems in the imported data.

evidence.finding: Long-range nonradiative quenching with approximately 28 nm half-quenching distance, rather than a universal sixth-power law.
evidence.reason: Donor identity and geometric distance convention were not verified from the accessible abstract; this radius cannot be assigned to vendor QDs.

evidence.finding: Gold size, arrangement and spectral overlap change QD lifetime and photon count rate. Enhancement and quenching require more than a universal radius.
evidence.reason: These coated dots and experimental geometries do not match the currently importable oleic-acid-coated vendor dots.

limitations: Rendered values are literature-based estimates, not sample-specific calibrations. The dye quantum yields, environment and linker geometry are assumed to match the reference experiment.
Between measured gold diameters, d0 is linearly interpolated as a display approximation. Gold size is never extrapolated outside the tabulated range.
Curves use donor-center-to-gold-surface distance in nm. The QD radius must not be subtracted from that distance.
The fitted distance law is evaluated at the scene separation; this does not establish experimental validity at every separation. Contact and overlap are not modeled.

Multiple acceptors are treated as independent added decay rates. Collective plasmon coupling, excitation enhancement, altered radiative rates, orientation, inner-filter effects and chemical quenching are not modeled.

Vendor spectrum images and emission peaks alone are insufficient to calculate a validated QD–gold radius. Uncalibrated pairs remain at reference brightness and are explicitly marked unknown, never zero quenching.
